questions.problem:
Given that $det(A)=14$, and $I$ is the $3\times 3$ identity matrix, which of the following statements are true?

- $\text{det}(A)-\text{det}(3I)=-13$
- $-\text{det}({A}^{T})+\text{det}(I)=-13$
- $\text{det}(A)-\text{det}({A}^{T})=-28$
questions.worked_solution:
From the properties of determinants, we know that 

$$
\text{det}({A}^{T})=\text{det}(A)=14
$$

and

$$
det(I)=1.
$$

Now, notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}3I & =3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a diagonal matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}| & ={3}^{3}=27.\end{aligned}
$$

With that in mind, let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed,

$$
\text{det}(A)-\text{det}(3I)=14-27=-13
$$

- Statement II is true. Indeed,

$$
-\text{det}({A}^{T})+\text{det}(I)=-14+1=-13
$$

- Statement III is false. We have

$$
\text{det}(A)-\text{det}({A}^{T})=14-14=0\ne -28
$$

In conclusion, the correct answer is "I and II only".

questions.problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$F=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -2 \\ 4 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the $3$rd column contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(F) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -2 \\ 4 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}| & =-1\cdot (3\cdot (-1)\cdot (-3))=-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
det(F)=-9.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$H=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 7 & \,\,\,-3 & 8 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 10 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the $3$rd row contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $3$rd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(H) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 7 & \,\,\,-3 & 8 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 10 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & \,\,\,-3 & 8 \\ 10 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & \,\,\,-3 & 8 \\ 10 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the $1$st row of the $3\times 3$ determinant contains two zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(H) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & -3 & 8 \\ 10 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}-3 & 8 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & 8 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(-6-0) \\  & =3\cdot (-6) \\  & =-18.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that $det(A)=3$, which of the following statements are true? 

- $-4\text{det}({A}^{T})+2\text{det}(I)=3$
- $2\text{det}({A}^{T})=6$
- $\text{det}({A}^{T})-\text{det}(I)=1$
questions.worked_solution:
From the properties of determinants, we know that 

$$
\text{det}({A}^{T})=\text{det}(A)=3
$$

and

$$
det(I)=1.
$$

With that in mind, let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false. Indeed,

$$
-4\text{det}({A}^{T})+2\text{det}(I)=-4\cdot 3+2\cdot 1=-10\ne 3.
$$

- Statement II is true. We have

$$
2\text{det}({A}^{T})=2\cdot 3=6.
$$

- Statement III is false. We have

$$
\text{det}({A}^{T})-\text{det}(I)=3-1=2\ne 1.
$$

In conclusion, the correct answer is "II only."

questions.problem:
Calculate the volume of the $4$-dimensional parallelepiped spanned by the vectors

$$
a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 7 \\ 5 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,c=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 10 \\ 0 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,d=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's construct the matrix $M,$ whose columns are the coordinates of our vectors $a,$ $b,$ $c,$ and  $d:$

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 7 & 10 & 3 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 4 \\ -3 & 5 & 7 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The volume of the parallelepiped spanned by these vectors equals the absolute value of the determinant of $M:$

$$
V=|det(M)|
$$

Notice that the $1$st row of the determinant contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 7 & 10 & 3 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 4 \\ -3 & 5 & 7 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}-2 & 10 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 \\ -3 & 7 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}-2 & 10 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 \\ -3 & 7 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the $2$nd row of the $3\times 3$ determinant contains two zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =-2|\begin{aligned}-2 & 10 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 \\ -3 & 7 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2\cdot 4\cdot (-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}-2 & 10 \\ -3 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =8|\begin{aligned}-2 & 10 \\ -3 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =8(-14+30) \\  & =128.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume is

$$
V=|det(M)|=|128|=128.
$$
